name: Coroado
confidence_why: Coroado is extinct and known only from nineteenth-century wordlists (Martius 1867 and earlier travellers), and the one work that addresses accent, Loukotka 1937, says outright that no general stress rule can be established for the family and offers penultimate (sometimes final) stress only as a hypothesis, while Silva Neto 2007 says nothing about stress.
catalog_citation: Loukotka, Čestmír. 1937. La familia lingüística Coroado. Journal de la Société des Américanistes 29(1): 157-214. doi:10.3406/jsa.1937.1952
catalog_locator: Section 'Fonética', p. 161 (last paragraph) to p. 162 (first paragraph); Persée page renders loukotka1937_pages/ and (assembled); scanned in
catalog_quote: Como hemos dicho, todos los vocabularios que tenemos a nuestra disposición son antiguos y ninguno ha sido establecido según las normas de la fonética moderna. Por consiguiente, es totalmente imposible determinar el sonido y la articulación de las vocales así como de las consonantes. Todo lo referido aquí en cuanto a la fonética y acentuación tiene por consiguiente un carácter hipotético. No es posible establecer una regla general para la acentuación en los idiomas de esta familia, parece probable que el acento tónico racae sobre la penúltima sílaba y en ciertos casos sobre la última. Resulta también muy difícil decidir si una vocal se breve o larga. Todos nuestros datos al respecto son dudosos.
world_status: statement found in an open source

new_statements.translation: As we have said, all the vocabularies at our disposal are old and none was recorded according to the norms of modern phonetics. [...] Everything stated here regarding phonetics and accentuation is therefore hypothetical. It is not possible to establish a general rule for accentuation in the languages of this family; it seems probable that the tonic accent falls on the penultimate syllable and in certain cases on the last. It is also very difficult to decide whether a vowel is short or long. All our data in this respect are doubtful.

new_statements.rule_in_words: Tentatively, word stress on the penultimate syllable, with some words stressed on the final syllable; the author explicitly says no general rule can be established and that the inference (from accent marks in pre-phonetic 19th-century wordlists of Coroado, Puri and Koropó) is hypothetical.
new_statements.exceptions: 'en ciertos casos sobre la última' — final stress in some items; no conditioning given. Vowel length also undeterminable.
new_statements.domain_note: Family-level remark (Coroado + Puri + Koropó jointly) inferred from isolated citation forms in 19th-c. wordlists (Eschwege 1818/1830, Saint-Hilaire 1830, Martius 1867 incl. Marlière's Aldeia da Pedra list, Ferreira-Moutinho 1869, Torrezão 1889); word-level accent as marked by the collectors, not phrase-level; not specific to Coroado alone.
new_statements.identity_note: Loukotka's accent remark is made for the whole 'familia Coroado' (Coroado docs C1–C5: Rio Xipotó and Aldeia da Pedra/Marlière lists, Saint-Hilaire, Eschwege, Ferreira-Moutinho; Puri P1–P4 = Glottolog puri1262; Koropó K1–K3 = Glottolog koro1298, now usually classed as Maxakalían), not for Coroado (coro1249) alone. The language is extinct and attested only in pre-phonetic 19th-century wordlists (Glottolog Glottolog's most extensive description = wordlist or less), so no first-hand description of stress from fieldwork exists or can exist; the modern 'Pury/Puri' retomada variety (Santos-Lopes 2024, Gamito 2016) is a reconstructed revival language filed under puri1262.
